definitions.coverage: legitimate paraphrases read as a claim (any type)
definitions.uncommon_coverage: held-out uncommon legitimate wording read as its own type (written and labelled before the classifier was run on it; see the category note)
definitions.false_negative_rate: legitimate claims (paraphrases + held-out uncommon wording) NOT read as their own type: abstained (held for a human) or misread
definitions.false_positive_rate: ambiguous, unsupported and contradictory messages read confidently as a claim
definitions.misclassification_rate: of every message read as a claim, the share read as a type other than the labelled one (incl. claims where an abstain or non-claim was expected)
definitions.abstain_rate: share of all messages on which the classifier abstained (fail-safe to a human)
definitions.adversarial_wrong_type_rate: attack prose read as a claim type other than the one it asserts

kinds.all: synthetic (hand-authored phrasings; the benchmark and the classifier share an author)

category_notes.uncommon_legitimate: held-out: written and labelled in the 2.2.0 review before the classifier was run on it. First run, with the classifier as of commit 9693433: 7/21 recognised, 14 abstained, 0 misread. The patterns were then extended against the separate development set, by an author who had seen those 14 misses, so the current number is optimistic; the remaining misses were deliberately not fitted
category_notes.development: written after the held-out run and used to extend the patterns: a fit, not an estimate

frozen.name: claims-frozen-2026-10-01
frozen.provenance: Written and labelled on 2026-10-01 by the same author (an AI assistant) who maintains the classifier, BEFORE the classifier was run on any of it, and committed before the first run. It must never be used to change the classifier: a miss here is reported, not fixed. It is partially informed (its author has seen the classifier's patterns), so it is not a blind test.

methodology.dataset: seven categories of dispute phrasings, incl. a held-out set of uncommon legitimate wording and the development set used to extend the patterns
methodology.method: each phrasing classified once against its label; false negatives over legitimate categories, false positives over ambiguous / unsupported / contradictory
methodology.limitations: the benchmark and the classifier share an author; a regression floor, not a generalisation claim; the held-out number after the pattern change is optimistic (the author had seen the first-run misses)
